bug_semantics: CRuby Nokogiri::XSLT::Stylesheet#transform (ext/nokogiri/xslt_stylesheet.c) heap-allocates a NULL-terminated const char** params array, then converts each Ruby transform parameter with StringValueCStr before xsltApplyStylesheet. StringValueCStr raises ArgumentError on an embedded NUL; that raise skipped free/ruby_xfree of the array, leaking about 24–32 bytes per call. Attacker-controlled transform params containing null bytes can therefore grow RSS in a long-running process (CWE-401 DoS). The transform still raises as expected and does not corrupt memory. JRuby is unaffected. Fixed in 1.19.3 by populating params under rb_protect and ruby_xfree'ing before rb_jump_tag.
flaw_origin: The calloc/ruby_xcalloc of the params array without an exception-safe free existed since the 2008 transform implementation, but a Ruby string with an embedded NUL did not raise and the array was always freed. The leak-on-NUL mechanism was first written in d20552c9a3e3def794bb9a74e6f14cab64b5342a (Lars Kanis, PR sparklemotion/nokogiri#1381): that commit changed the transform loop from StringValuePtr to StringValueCStr. Immediate parent f5a9dc9a8e0f7579be86909685e56643db96a351 still uses StringValuePtr in that loop and has zero StringValueCStr in xslt_stylesheet.c. Later ruby_xcalloc/rename/style commits carried the same CStr-after-alloc pattern until the 1.19.3 rb_protect fix.
